messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — we have ~$120k in promo credits for account redwood-prod expiring 2026-05-03. Can these credits be applied to Dedicated reserved commitments or are they restricted to hosted usage? Need answers before we finalize next-quarter committed GPUs.

sam: Are these promo codes tied to billing account or project? If project-scoped they likely only offset hosted API charges. org-level credits might cover committed invoices but vendor terms vary.

maya: Billing dashboard shows them under "promo" and attached to billing-account BC-984. Details are sparse. Also worried: if credits disappear, we'll exceed committed thresholds and fall into on-demand for a short window, which will spike cloud spend.

billing-bot: notice: PromoCredit BC-984-APR2026 amount=120000 currency=USD expires=2026-05-03 scope=billing_account eligible_usage=[hosted_api,embeddings] not_eligible=[reserved_commitments]

oliver: That's unfortunate — billing-bot suggests reserved_commitments not eligible. If that's true, Dedicated invoices won't be covered.

priya: I'll escalate to CloudAM (support ticket) now. Quick ask: can finance show last 6 months of usage split hosted vs dedicated so we can model impact if credits vanish?

maya: Posting numbers from our cost-export (last 6 months): hosted_api=45% cost, dedicated_reserved=50%, other=5%. With $120k gone, hosted would be most impacted but dedicated invoices still high.

sam: Operational idea — if credits only cover hosted, we can temporarily move some batch workloads from hosted to Dedicated / spot to reduce hosted bill until credits expire. But need to check SLAs.

oliver: We can also enable aggressive batching and lower max tokens for background jobs. Expected reduction ~15-25% token cost. Not ideal but viable short-term.

priya: Ticket created: CLOUD-6482 to ask for promo scope extension OR conversion to org-level credit. Escalated to account rep. Copying the support snippet I sent:

`````
Hello — our promo credit BC-984 expires 2026-05-03. We request either a 30-day grace or conversion to organization-level credit to apply against reserved commitment invoices. Account: redwood-prod (billing account BC-984). Contact: priya@redwood.com
`````

maya: Finance will prepare contingency budget: assume credits don't apply to dedicated. Plan: 1) short-term workload rerouting 2) enable cost-saver quantization on non-prod 3) ask sales to pause non-essential dedicated capacity spin-ups.

sam: I'll draft an infra runbook for moving workloads and throttling nonessential pipelines. Will tag @oliver for the batching knobs.

oliver: I'll put a PR on routing policies and add a feature flag to divert non-critical inference to cheaper models.

priya: Support replied (email): "We're reviewing. Promo credits generally target usage charges; reserved commitment invoices excluded by default. We can request exception but not guaranteed." :cry: 

maya: Ok — assume worst case. Action items: finance to rebalance budgets, infra to prepare workload moves, sales to notify any customers impacted by capacity changes. We'll reconvene Thu 16:00 UTC.

sam: :thumbsup: 

oliver: :eyes: 

priya: Will update CLOUD-6482 with support thread and estimated delta once I have vendor confirmation.

maya: Thanks all — tagging this for exec visibility.
